name: The Balance of Nature
summary: Conservator Ilthalaine sends defenders into Shadowglen to thin its growing wildlife. Mature thistle boars and mangy nightsabers threaten the glade's balance.

sections.title: A Burden of Stewardship
sections.body: Shadowglen's adult animals now threaten the World Tree's ecosystem. Conservator Ilthalaine sends young defenders deeper into the forest to hunt mature thistle boars and older, mangy nightsabers. Their appetites can exhaust the land's limited plants and game.

sections.title: Predator and Prey
sections.body: North of Aldrassil, younger cubs give way to mottled nightsabers and aggressive boars that root through the soil. For kaldorei, controlled hunting is a grim duty, but it protects the whole forest from collapse.

faq.q: Why is Conservator Ilthalaine having these beasts culled?
faq.answer: Without intervention, growing numbers of thistle boars and nightsabers could strip Shadowglen of vital resources. The land would be left barren and unable to sustain life on Teldrassil's boughs.

faq.q: Where are the mangy nightsabers and thistle boars located?
faq.answer: The mangy nightsabers and thistle boars roam northern Shadowglen, past Aldrassil's boughs. Look for spotted coats on the nightsabers; younger cubs closer to the sanctuary have stripes.
Conservator Ilthalaine cares for Shadowglen and oversees the health of Teldrassil's starting glade. She guides newly awakened night elves in keeping the forest in balance.

faq.q: How does this fit into night elf beliefs about nature?
faq.answer: Night elves honor nature, and stewardship means managing overgrowth. When one species grows too numerous and starves out others, the whole forest suffers; culling is a sorrowful but vital duty.

faq.q: Is this the end of the Balance of Nature chain?
aliases: what comes after balance of nature
faq.answer: This is the second and final step in the initial Balance of Nature chain. Other work soon addresses the deeper, more unnatural corruption troubling Teldrassil's wildlife.

faq.q: Why are the nightsabers described as mangy?
aliases: what is wrong with the sabers
faq.answer: Older, rougher nightsabers roam the glade's fringes, where their numbers strain Shadowglen's food supply. Many grow scruffy and aggressive.

angles.text: For young night elves, this is an early lesson in the harsh demands of caring for the wilderness on Teldrassil.
Druidic teachings prize harmony over sentiment. Thinning overgrown packs preserves the great web of life.
Taking down swift sabers and stubborn boars teaches you to track and thin their numbers, skills needed to keep nature in balance.
